subject: MAP-driven reservation pricing and burst agreement
messages:
From: Alice Moreno <alice@stellarretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Eval plan + dedicated reservation sizing

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked solid for our peak checkout flows. We had two asks from the platform and procurement teams as we scope an evaluation:

- We need a short MAP (mutual action plan) showing milestones for POC -> pilot -> production and expected deliverables at each step.
- An initial recommendation for GPU pool sizing (expected peak concurrent sessions ~180, typical seq len 256) and what reserve/commit options make sense for a 6–12 month evaluation.

Procurement would also like to understand: ramp triggers for pricing discounts (e.g., hitting X qps for 30 days) and any burst allowances if we temporarily exceed reserved capacity during seasonal spikes.

Can you share a draft MAP and a rough pricing band so we can estimate TCO for the POC? We can loop in contracts after we see the draft.

—Alice
Alice Moreno
Head of Product Operations | Stellar Retail
alice@stellarretail.com

P.S. attaching our internal capacity planning spreadsheet in a follow-up (will send from procurement).

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice@stellarretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval plan + dedicated reservation sizing

Hi Alice — really appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass MAP and a sizing proposal (MAP-draft_StellarRetail_v1.pdf). Summary below so procurement has a quick reference: 

Summary (TL;DR)
- Proposed evaluation term: 90-day POC -> 90-day pilot -> production (option to convert at month 6)
- Recommended GPU pool: 10 x A100-style instances (quantization-friendly), burst pool + autoscale for short spikes
- Pricing bands: 3 tiers based on committed GPUs and term length (6m, 12m, 24m); sample: 6m commit = $X per GPU/hr, 12m commit = -12% from list, 24m commit = -20% from list
- Ramp-triggered discounts: sustained usage over 30 days that exceeds 80% of reserved throughput unlocks an incremental discount (applies to subsequent billing period)
- Burst clause: short bursts (<= 48 hours) up to +30% capacity available at no surcharge; longer bursts billed at pre-agreed burst rate (or fall back to hosted pool if capacity constrained)

Next steps I propose:
1) You and procurement review draft MAP and sizing.
2) We refine pricing tiers with Marcus (cc'd) — Marcus will run a few sensitivity scenarios.
3) If acceptable, we produce a mutual SLA addendum + DocuSign-ready SOW.

Attachments: MAP-draft_StellarRetail_v1.pdf

Best,
Soojin Lee

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Eval plan + dedicated reservation sizing — pricing input needed

Team — forwarding Alice's asks and the MAP draft. Quick notes and questions for pricing/ops: 

- Customer expected peak concurrent sessions ~180. I recommended 10 GPUs as a starting point; can we confirm that maps to ~2000 tokens/s aggregated throughput with our quantized profile?
- They asked for a 6–12 month evaluation; they prefer converting to production at month 6 if metrics look good.
- They want a "no-surcharge" burst allowance for very short spikes (<=48h) up to +30% capacity; beyond that, they want predictable burst pricing or automatic fallback to hosted pool.

Marcus — can you run:
- Two sizing sensitivity runs (10 GPUs, 14 GPUs) with cost per token estimates and expected latency under 95th percentile.
- Proposed discount schedule for 6m vs 12m vs 24m commits; include a ramp-trigger clause: e.g., 10% extra discount after X sustained throughput for 30 days.

Laura — if this escalates to procurement redlines, can you flag any standard legal 'burst' language we should avoid (e.g., open-ended credits)?

Thanks,
Soojin

From: Procurement Team <contracts@procureit.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Alice Moreno <alice@stellarretail.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP-draft and SOW — redlines and burst clause question

Hi Soojin / Alice,

Thanks for the MAP. We've attached an initial SOW with redlines (Stellar_SOW_Draft.docx). A few open items:

1) Burst allowance: the customer requests a guaranteed free burst window of 72 hours per quarter up to +40% of reserved capacity.
- Can Redwood support a guaranteed 72-hour quarterly buffer at no charge? If not, we need clear pricing when that buffer is used.

2) Ramp discount trigger: they want the discount to apply retroactively to the month where the trigger was hit, rather than forward-looking. Is that feasible?

3) Term conversion: they want an automatic conversion from evaluation to production after month 6 unless either party opts out with 30 days' notice.

Please respond with proposed contractual language for these items so procurement can move to signature.

Regards,
Procurement Team
contracts@procureit.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice@stellarretail.com>, Procurement Team <contracts@procureit.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Final MAP + reservation terms proposal

Hi Alice / Procurement — thanks for the redlines. We've reviewed internally and put together language that should be workable for both sides. High level changes below; I've attached an updated MAP and a DocuSign-ready SOW link.

Key commercial points (proposed)
- Evaluation cadence: 90-day POC -> 90-day pilot -> option to convert to production at month 6. Either party may opt out with 30 days' notice before conversion.
- Reservation sizing: initial committed pool = 12 GPUs (A100-equivalent, quantization profile Q4_8). This maps to expected 95th-pctl latency under your stated load; Marcus validated both 10 and 14 GPU scenarios and recommended 12 as a balanced starting point.
- Term and discounts: 12-month reserved term recommended for production conversion. Discount schedule: 6m commit = baseline price; 12m commit = -12%; 24m commit = -20%.
- Ramp-triggered discount: when sustained usage >80% of reserved throughput for any 30 consecutive days, a 5% retroactive credit will be applied to usage charges for that 30-day window (credit applied in the following invoice).
- Burst clause: 72-hour quarterly free burst up to +30% of reserved capacity (we compromise from +40% to +30%). Additional burst beyond that will be billed at pre-agreed burst rate (1.8x list) or overflow to Redwood hosted pool if dedicated capacity is exhausted. We also include an option for scheduled temporary capacity increases with 7 days' notice.
- SLA & fallbacks: if dedicated pool is unavailable for >6 hours, requests will be routed to hosted pool; Redwood will provide pro-rated credits for impacted requests per SLA schedule.

Next concrete steps:
1) Review the attached updated SOW (DocuSign link below). If language is good, sign and we will provision the reserved pool within 10 business days of signature.
2) If you want a stronger burst allowance, we can build that into a priced addendum instead of changing the base contract.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/track?doc=XR-8923-stellar
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-7892

Attachments: MAP-draft_StellarRetail_v1.pdf, Stellar_SOW_Draft.docx

Looking forward — happy to hop on a short call to walk through the final points.

Best,
